# EnterpriseGlue v0.35.10 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.35.9`.

## Highlights

- **release-authorization:** Resume frozen toolchain distribution publication without changing its authenticated original receipt or immutable lock.
- **mission-control:** Resolve opaque process-definition identifiers in instance lists and verify live process existence before reading variables.

## User and administrator impact

- A failed publisher can complete the same qualified release while preserving its original toolchain receipt and immutable distribution lock.
- Operators can distinguish a missing release attachment from an unknown registry or signature failure.
- Active and completed instance lists support engine-generated opaque definition IDs.
- Missing or completed runtime processes return not-found for variable reads.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Install the reviewed protected publication controls, then use the existing frozen-source recovery protocol. No application, package or database upgrade is introduced by this control repair.
- Upgrade the backend host package or host image through the ordinary release process.

## API and integration compatibility

- Existing instance-list and variable-read behavior is restored.
- OpenAPI now includes the existing tenant-scoped list route with its required engine selector, authentication and error contracts.

## Configuration

- Candidate-backed toolchain publication loads recovery controls from the exact protected workflow revision while keeping the qualified source checkout unchanged.
- The original authenticated toolchain receipt remains in the distribution; the current attempt receipt is retained separately.
- An explicitly authorized recovery still requires the frozen source and reviewed recovery_prs, with renewed current security acceptance.
- The existing publisher static-contract checker is included in the narrowly reviewed publication-repair path list and runs in the fast publication regression gate. Scanner policy, manifests, lockfiles, Dockerfiles and payload paths remain excluded.

## Database migrations

- This publication-only change modifies no application runtime or database schema.
- No schema or data migration.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: yes.

## Security

- The existing distribution must independently verify against the fixed protected toolchain signer and GitHub OIDC issuer before its receipt is used. Source, version, images, charts and archive hashes must match the qualified candidate; any content drift stops publication.
- Signature visibility handling retries only the same bounded verification read when the exact missing-signature diagnostic is returned. Invalid signatures, access failures and unknown registry responses stop immediately; signing is never retried by this helper.
- Published semantic tags and immutable locks are never replaced. Only a definite absent distribution permits first-publication receipt creation.
- Authorization, runtime tenant filters and variable redaction are preserved. An engine error is classified as not-found only after a typed parent lookup proves absence.

## Documentation

- The artifact-promotion runbook describes original-receipt custody, separate attempt provenance and bounded signature verification.
- docs/development/mission-control-engine-selection.md

## Known limitations

- Local wire fixtures do not establish protected publisher acceptance. The non-publishing canary and exact frozen-source recovery must pass before declaring publication complete.
- Publication does not establish staging installation, routing, tenant qualification or production readiness.
- Partially uploaded distribution attachment sets require independent reconciliation of existing bytes before another publisher retry. Only complete absence is classified as recoverable missing attachments.
- Real engine, browser and protected release acceptance remain required before publication.

## Rollback

- Revert the publication controls and stop new recovery dispatches. Preserve existing releases, semantic tags, signed receipts and immutable locks.
- Restore the previous host image using the ordinary guarded deployment process.

## Validation evidence

- Local publication-record, approval, batch and non-publishing authorization regressions pass, including shallow-source control extraction, run-provenance drift, exact promoted chart namespaces, corrupt payloads and bounded signature reads.
- The real public-registry read independently verifies the existing distribution signature and preserves its original receipt while matching the exact candidate source, image and chart bindings. This is read-only evidence, not protected publisher acceptance.
- The expanded CI contract gate and self-validating aggregate, deterministic classifier fixtures, publisher policy checks and Actionlint pass. Protected CI, the required non-publishing canary and actual frozen-source recovery remain required.
- Targeted service, route, schema and authorization regression checks.
